\section{The product
  formula}\label{sec:product}

Throughout, $\primes$ denotes the set of primes and $s$ a real number.

\begin{defn}[Zeta function]\label{def:zeta}
For $s > 1$ let $\zeta(s) = \sum_{n \in \N} n^{-s}$.
\end{defn}

\begin{assum}[Unique factorisation]\label{assum:ufd}
Every integer $n \ge 2$ is a product of primes, and the product is unique
up to the order of its factors.
\end{assum}

\begin{lem}\label{lem:geometric}
For every prime $p$ and every $s > 1$,
\[
  \frac{1}{1 - p^{-s}} = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} p^{-ks},
\]
and the series converges absolutely.
\end{lem}

\begin{proof}
Since $p \ge 2$ and $s > 1$, the ratio $p^{-s}$ lies in $(0, 1/2]$; the
geometric series converges absolutely.

Its sum is $1/(1 - p^{-s})$ by the usual formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{restatable}[Euler product]{thm}{eulerproduct}\label{thm:euler-product}
For every $s > 1$ the product $\prod_{p \in \primes} (1 - p^{-s})^{-1}$
converges and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:euler-product}
  \zeta(s) = \prod_{p \in \primes} \frac{1}{1 - p^{-s}}.
\end{equation}
\end{restatable}

We postpone the proof to \cref{app:proofs}, after a remark on what the
finite products count.

\begin{proofsketch}
Multiply out the geometric series of \cref{lem:geometric} and let the
bound on the primes grow.
\end{proofsketch}

\begin{rem}
Let $P_x(s) = \prod_{p \le x} (1 - p^{-s})^{-1}$. Multiplying out the
finitely many series of \cref{lem:geometric}, each term $n^{-s}$ of
$P_x(s)$ belongs to an $n$ all of whose prime factors are at most $x$, and
by \cref{assum:ufd} it appears exactly once.\footnote{The order of the
  factors does not matter: the series are absolutely convergent
  (\cref{lem:geometric}).} The tail of $\zeta(s)$ missing from $P_x(s)$ is
\label{eq:tail}
\[
  0 \le \zeta(s) - P_x(s) \le \sum_{n > x} n^{-s}.
\]
which tends to zero as $x \to \infty$.
\end{rem}

\begin{example}
For $s = 2$ the product formula gives $\prod_p (1 - p^{-2})^{-1} = \pi^2/6$.
\end{example}

{\bf A consequence.} Since every factor of the product exceeds one, no
factor vanishes, and $\zeta(s) > 0$ for every $s > 1$.
